text:
Predicates:
Visited(x, y) ::: x visited y.
MountainRange(y) ::: y is a mountain range.
LocatedIn(y, z) ::: y is located in z.
Mine(x) ::: x is a mine.
Donated(x) ::: x has been donated.
InRangeIn(x, y) ::: x is a mountain range in y.
HasMine(x) ::: x has a mine.

Premises:
PicurisMountains(y) ∧ MountainRange(y) ∧ LocatedIn(y, NewMexico) ∨ LocatedIn(y, Texas) ::: The Picuris Mountains are a mountain range in New Mexico or Texas.
Visited(Juan, y) ::: Juan de Onate visited the Picuris Mountains.
Mine(earth) ∧ LocatedIn(earth, y) ∧ Donated(earth) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine, located in the Picuris Mountains, was donated.
¬∃x (MountainRange(x) ∧ LocatedIn(x, Texas) ∧ HasMine(x) ∧ Donated(x)) ::: There are no mountain ranges in Texas that have mines which have been donated.

Conclusion:
Visited(Juan, y) ∧ LocatedIn(y, Texas) ::: Juan de Onate visited a mountain range in Texas.
